title: Leaf count after pruning a subprotocol
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol and let $s$ be a subprotocol of $p$, that is, a rooted subtree of $p$. Write $L(q)$ for the number of leaves (output nodes) of a protocol $q$, and suppose that $L(s) < L(p)$. Then the protocol obtained by pruning $s$ out of $p$ has exactly $L(p) - L(s)$ leaves.
hypotheses_covered: the number of leaves of $s$ is strictly less than the number of leaves of $p$
